query_used: Downloaded the 149-page roster PDF; extracted text (pdfplumber, p.64); full-text scan for HUBBELL variants.

raw_record.verbatim: HUBBELL, JAMES.—Age, 22 years. Enlisted in Seventh Congressional District, to serve three years, and mustered in as private, Co. I, March 9, 1864; promoted corporal in May, 1864; wounded in action, October 19, 1864, at Cedar Creek, Va.; mustered out with company, October 2, 1865, at Savannah, Ga.
raw_record.ocr_note: OCR rendered 'May, 1864' as 'May, 1861' and similar digit slips elsewhere; the name/company/Cedar-Creek line is clean.

parsed.name: James Hubbell
parsed.fate_in_roster: mustered out (death Oct 1865 post-dates this record)

candidates.claude_reasoning: C1 (dispositive in combination): Co. I, 153rd NY matches; exactly ONE 'HUBBELL, JAMES' in the regiment. C2: enlistment Mar 1864 and the Cedar Creek wound (Oct 19 1864) inside the window. C7: same Co. I as confirmed brother Charles F. Hubbell. C6: corporal matches the letters' 'lance corporal drilling recruits.' Disambiguated from the two unrelated Co. E (Minden) Hubbells and from Charles (enlisted Aug 1862). NOTE: the roster records muster-out Oct 2 1865, NOT his death at Albany Oct 12 1865 — the death post-dates the AG record (see grave-death.json).
